newsitem.title: THAILAND: Merrill Lynch says Thai debt concern misplaced.
newsitem.headline: Merrill Lynch says Thai debt concern misplaced.

text.p: Merrill Lynch said on Tuesday a recent decision by Moody's Investor Services to downgrade Thailand's short-term foreign debt was misplaced given its strong fiscal and monetary positions.

Merrill Lynch said Thailand's short-term debt problem has been alleviated by a move by its central bank several months ago to require banks to set aside seven percent cash reserves on short-term borrowing.

It said due to a new government emerging after Thai election this month, the Bank of Thailand was highly unlikely to change its practice of daily fixing the baht against a basket of currencies before mid-1997.
"It would seem the risk of a forced devaluation is low, especially now that we think we are past the peak in the current account imbalance and the short-term debt buildup."

Merrill Lynch said Thai interest rates could ease by 200 basis points by mid-1997 if government uncertainty disappeared after the November 17 poll and Thai current account and trade deficits continued narrowing.

It said Thailand's clouded political picture, slow improvement on its external imbalance and market fears of a baht devaluation have limited a decline in baht interest rates in the past several months.
